mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -73.0 to -37.6, indicates a sustained recovery trend that will continue over the next four weeks as consumer confidence and willingness to engage in non-essential activities grow.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, indicating a halt or reversal of the recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant and sustained increase in PARKS mobility, now well above baseline at +19.3%, suggests a general increase in outdoor activity and willingness to leave home, which will spill over into retail and recreation. If PARKS remains above +15%, RETAIL_REC will continue to rise over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS drops below +15% or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS remaining high over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, both showing consistent week-over-week increases, indicates a return to daily commuting patterns. This directly increases opportunities for retail and recreation activities during commutes or lunch breaks, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to rise, but RETAIL_REC stagnates or falls over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from +24.6% to +14.9%, coupled with increases across other categories, strongly suggests an ongoing easing of stay-at-home orders or public health recommendations. This directly enables and encourages more out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases or stabilizes, but RETAIL_REC does not respond positively over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM mobility approaches its baseline (currently -10.0%), it signals a broader return to essential out-of-home activities, which often precedes or accompanies a return to non-essential retail and recreation. If GROCERY_PHARM crosses -5%, RETAIL_REC will accelerate its recovery over the next week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM crosses -5% but RETAIL_REC does not show an accelerated recovery over the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of increasing PARKS mobility (now +19.3%) and decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility (now +14.9%) indicates a strong shift in public behavior towards spending more time outside the home for leisure and recreation, which will naturally extend to retail and recreation venues over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS continues to rise and RESIDENTIAL continues to fall, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in TRANSIT mobility, from -61.1% to -44.3%, reflects a growing comfort with public transportation and increased movement across the city. This is a prerequisite for higher retail and recreation engagement and will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC stagnates or falls over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a return to pre-pandemic work-life routines. People spending less time at home and more time commuting and working creates more opportunities for retail and recreation during the workday or commute, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks.
